source: Pew Research Center Political Typology Quiz (2021 edition)
SCORING_UNAVAILABLE: Items only. The 2021 quiz shipped no point weights or per-group response rates in its markup; the 2025-era page was a React app fed by an API that no longer resolves; the live quiz API 404s for the retired quiz id; and the 169-page 2021 report publishes TOPLINE percentages only, not per-option percentages by typology group. Without P(answer|group) neither the ideology score nor the naive-Bayes group assignment used for the 2026 edition can be computed. These items can be administered, but the answers cannot be mapped to a 2021 typology group.

items.text: If you had to choose, would you rather have…

options.text: > A smaller government providing fewer services
> A bigger government providing more services

items.text: When you say you favor a bigger government providing more services, do you think it would be better to…

options.text: > Modestly expand on current government services
> Greatly expand on current government services

items.text: Which of the following statements come closest to your view?

options.text: > America’s openness to people from all over the world is essential to who we are as a nation
> If America is too open to people from all over the world, we risk losing our identity as a nation

items.text: In general, would you say experts who study a subject for many years are…
Thinking about increased trade of goods and services between the U.S. and other nations in recent decades, would you say that the U.S. has…

options.text: > Gained more than it has lost because increased trade has helped lower prices and increased the competitiveness of some U.S. businesses
> Lost more than it has gained because increased trade has cost jobs in manufacturing and other industries and lowered wages for some U.S. workers

items.text: How much more, if anything, needs to be done to ensure equal rights for all Americans regardless of their racial or ethnic backgrounds?
Which comes closer to your view about what needs to be done to ensure equal rights for all Americans regardless of their racial or ethnic backgrounds — even if neither is exactly right?

options.text: > Most U.S. laws and major institutions need to be completely rebuilt because they are fundamentally biased against some racial and ethnic groups
> While there are many inequities in U.S. laws and institutions, necessary changes can be made by working within the current systems

items.text: Which of the following statements comes closest to your view?

options.text: > Business corporations make too much profit
> Most corporations make a fair and reasonable amount of profit

items.text: How much, if at all, would it bother you to regularly hear people speak a language other than English in public places in your community?
Which of these statements best describes your opinion about the United States?

options.text: > The U.S. stands above all other countries in the world
> The U.S. is one of the greatest countries in the world, along with some others
> There are other countries that are better than the U.S.

items.text: People being too easily offended by things others say
People saying things that are very offensive to others
Which comes closer to your view of candidates for political office, even if neither is exactly right? I usually feel like…

options.text: > There is at least one candidate who shares most of my views
> None of the candidates represent my views well

items.text: In general, how much do White people benefit from advantages in society that Black people do not have?
Do you think greater social acceptance of people who are transgender (people who identify as a gender that is different from the sex they were assigned at birth) is…

options.text: > Neither good nor bad for society

items.text: Overall, would you say people who are convicted of crimes in this country serve…

options.text: > About the right amount of time in prison

items.text: In the future, do you think…

options.text: > U.S. policies should try to keep it so America is the only military superpower
> It would be acceptable if another country became as militarily powerful as the U.S.
